title: The Bible in a minute

line.younger: The whole Bible as one story, short enough to share, in eight pictures along one road.
line.older: One book, one story: the whole Bible from creation to the new creation, short enough to share, in eight pictures along one road.

poster: A garden's great tree stands on the left and a walled city with its gate on the right, with a faint path between them. Along the foot of the picture a road runs from left to right, with a faint ring for each of its thirteen stops.

frames.name: Made good
frames.still: A garden under the sun: a great tree, a palm, a river, sheep grazing, a bird in the air, and two people standing among the plants. On the road below, the first stop appears.
frames.younger: God made everything, and it was very good. He made people to know him and to take care of his world.
frames.older: Before anything else, there is God. He speaks the world into being, calls it good, and makes people in his image to care for it.

frames.name: Broken
frames.still: The garden's wall, with its gate shut and a sword laid across it; the tree shows above the wall. Outside, on bare ground with thorns, two people walk away. The road reaches its second stop.
frames.younger: The first people did not trust God and did what he told them not to do. Sin and sadness came into the world.
frames.older: Adam and Eve reach for what God withheld, and the damage spreads. God judges, and he keeps showing mercy.

frames.name: A promise
frames.still: Night. A tent among the hills under a sky full of stars; a woman stands at the tent, and a man with a staff looks up. The road reaches its third stop.
frames.younger: God chose Abraham and promised him a family as many as the stars, and a blessing for the whole world.
frames.older: God calls one man and makes him a promise: a people, a land, and a blessing that will reach every family on earth.

frames.name: A rescue
frames.still: Two panels. On the left, a dry path between two walls of water, with a family walking through. On the right, a mountain under a cloud, with the two tablets of the law at its foot. Two more stops appear on the road.
frames.younger: Abraham's family became slaves in Egypt. God set them free, led them through the sea, and gave them his good laws.
frames.older: Abraham's family has become a nation of slaves. God sets them free, opens a road through the sea, and gives the law at Sinai.

frames.name: A king
frames.still: Two panels. On the left, a house, a palm and standing grain in the land. On the right, a shepherd wearing a crown stands with his crook among his sheep. Two more stops appear on the road.
frames.younger: God brought his people into the land and gave them kings. He promised David that a king from his family would rule for ever.
frames.older: God gives the land, and Israel asks for a king. David loves God and fails badly too, and God promises him a son whose kingdom will never end.

frames.name: Exile, and hope
frames.still: Two panels. On the left, a city wall broken open with smoke above it, and people walking away carrying bundles. On the right, a lamp burning in the dark, an open scroll, and a wall being built again. Two more stops appear on the road.
frames.younger: The people stopped listening to God and were taken far from home. Prophets promised that God would not give up on them.
frames.older: The kingdom falls and Babylon burns Jerusalem. Yet the prophets promise a new covenant and a coming king, and the Old Testament ends looking ahead.

frames.name: Jesus: the cross and the empty tomb
frames.still: Two panels. On the left, Jesus stands by the lake with his arms open, teaching people who sit on the shore; a boat is on the water. On the right, a hill with a cross, and beside it an open tomb with its stone rolled away and light above it. Two more stops appear on the road.
frames.younger: God the Son was born as Jesus. He died on a cross to take away the sin of the world, and on the third day God raised him from the dead.
frames.older: God keeps his promises in person. Jesus dies on a Roman cross, carrying the sin of the world, and on the third day God raises him bodily from the dead.

frames.name: The Spirit, and all things new
frames.still: A city with its gate standing open and light pouring down on it. A river runs out from the gate past a great tree, and people walk toward the gate. The road is finished, with a flame for the Spirit on it too: every stop stands on it, from the garden to the city.
frames.younger: Jesus sent the Holy Spirit, and his followers told the good news everywhere. One day he will come back and make everything new.
frames.older: The Spirit comes and the church spreads to every nation. Jesus returns, death is undone, and God makes his home with people for ever.

verse.text: Behold, I make all things new.

think.younger: The road starts in a garden and ends in a city. What stays the same from the first stop to the last?
think.older: Where would you put yourself on this road? What has already happened, and what are Christians still waiting for?

care: This moving picture tells of a real death, Jesus' death on the cross. If it brings up fear or sadness, talk with a parent or a leader you trust, or look at Find Help.
